evals.name: recovers-intent-before-resolving
evals.prompt: git rebase onto main stopped with a conflict in src/auth/session.ts. sort it out
evals.expected_output: The conflicting hunks are read first, then the history behind each side — commit messages and the PR or issue that introduced them. Each hunk is resolved so both intents survive where they can coexist. The project's typecheck and tests are run afterwards, and the rebase is continued to the end.
expectations: Inspects the conflict state and the conflicting file before editing anything
Reads the commit messages, PR or issue behind both sides of at least one hunk
Resolves every conflict marker, leaving no <<<<<<< or >>>>>>> in the tree
Runs the project's typecheck and tests after resolving, before continuing
Continues the rebase until no commits are left to apply
anti_expectations: Runs git rebase --abort or git merge --abort
Picks a side without reading why either change was made
Adds behaviour that appears on neither side of the conflict
Continues the rebase while the project's checks are failing

evals.name: states-the-tradeoff-when-sides-are-incompatible
evals.prompt: both branches rewrote the retry logic in worker.ts differently and they can't both be right. what do we keep?
evals.expected_output: A resolution that names the merge's stated goal, keeps the side matching it, and reports the trade-off in one line: what the discarded side did and what is lost by dropping it.
expectations: Names which side was kept for the incompatible hunk and why
States what the discarded side accomplished and what is lost
Ties the choice to the goal of the merge rather than to recency or line count
anti_expectations: Invents a third behaviour that blends the two implementations
Keeps both code paths behind a new flag nobody asked for
Resolves the hunk silently, with no record of which intent was dropped

evals.name: verifies-with-the-projects-own-checks
evals.prompt: I fixed the conflict markers in the merge already. is it safe to commit?
evals.expected_output: The project's own commands are discovered — from orchestrate.config.json in a harness repo, otherwise from package.json or the equivalent — and typecheck, tests and format are run. Anything the merge broke is fixed before the merge is committed.
expectations: Discovers the project's check commands rather than assuming a command name
Runs typecheck and tests, and reports their actual output
Fixes what the merge broke before staging and committing
Confirms no conflict markers remain anywhere in the tree
anti_expectations: Calls the merge safe on the basis that the markers are gone
Reports the checks as passing without running them
Commits while a check is failing
